editorial:
Imagine taking one of the most famous shows ever and just deleting the main characters. That is exactly what happens here. You get to spend time with the background people of New York City right after the 1993 bombing. It feels like a weird, indie version of a sitcom where the side characters finally get the spotlight. You will follow Gunther as he tries to be less shy, and watch Carol and Susan deal with the stress of a new baby and a wedding. It turns a familiar world into something totally new and kind of strange, making you notice the little details you missed for years.

The editing is the real star here because it changes the whole mood of the scenes. The pacing feels slow and dreamy, which makes the small wins for these characters feel huge. While some parts might feel too quiet if you want a loud comedy, the mystery surrounding Dr. Farber keeps you guessing. You should definitely stream this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the background details, or maybe grab the 4K Blu-ray for your shelf if you love weird cinema experiments. It is a great pick for anyone who likes art projects.
endingExplained: The story wraps up with a surprising look at Dr. Farber. It turns out his dark secret was not as scary as you thought, but it showed how lonely he really was. Gunther finally makes a real friend outside of the coffee shop, giving him a win. The movie ends with a quiet shot of the city, showing that life goes on for the people we usually ignore in the background of other people's stories.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves odd art projects or the show Friends.
